name: Aberdeenshire
title: Aberdeenshire —
title_em: castles, whisky and the Highland Games.
tagline: More castles per acre than anywhere in Britain, plus Balmoral and the Braemar Gathering.
summary: Aberdeenshire stretches from the North Sea cliffs to the Cairngorms. It has the Castle Trail with more than a dozen castles, the Royal estate at Balmoral and a long working tradition of farming and fishing.
The Doric dialect is still heard here, and the region is the origin of many families who emigrated to Canada, the US and Australia.

famous_for.title: The Castle Trail
famous_for.text: Castles such as Crathes, Craigievar, Fyvie and Dunnottar.

famous_for.title: Balmoral and Royal Deeside
famous_for.text: The King's Highland home and the valley of the River Dee.

famous_for.title: Braemar Gathering
famous_for.text: One of the most famous Highland games, held every September.

places.name: Dunnottar Castle
places.text: A ruined clifftop fortress above the North Sea.

places.name: Crathes Castle
places.text: A 16th-century tower house with walled gardens.

places.name: Balmoral Castle
places.text: The Royal family's Highland home, open to visitors in summer.

festivals.name: Braemar Gathering
festivals.text: Caber tossing, hill racing and piping, often attended by the Royal family.

festivals.name: Stonehaven Fireballs
festivals.text: Locals swing fireballs through the streets at midnight.

sport.intro: The Highland League is a strong local football tradition, and the Highland Games are big events.

community.intro: Aberdeenshire people are strongly represented among Scots in Canada, the US and Australasia.

ancestry: Searching for your family's roots? ScotlandsPeople, the Scottish Government's genealogy service, holds statutory registers of births, marriages and deaths, census returns and Old Parish Registers.
